chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Suleiman ibn Khalid, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: When the thief steals, his hand is cut, and he is liable to compensate for what he took.
ai.seo_question: What is the penalty for theft in Shia jurisprudence according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the hadd of hand amputation for theft is not mutually exclusive with financial restitution (gharama), establishing a dual-penalty model where the thief suffers corporal punishment while also compensating the owner for the value of the stolen goods. This ruling is significant in Shia jurisprudence as it distinguishes between the punitive aspect of the hadd and the civil right of the owner to recover the asset's value, a point of discussion among scholars regarding whether the compensation is in addition to or part of the hadd execution.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Mansour Bin Hazim, from Suleyman Bin Khalid who said,
‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When thief steals, his hand it cut, and he has to compensate for whatever he has taken (stolen)’.
